thesis: NVIDIA remains the cash engine of the AI build-out: Q1 FY2027 (ended April 26, 2026) revenue $81.6B (+85% y/y), ~75% gross margin, record quarterly free cash flow of $49B, and Q2 guidance of $91B. Yet the stock is roughly flat for 2026 and trades at ~29.8x trailing earnings - the multiple has compressed while earnings exploded. Unlike the rest of the AI complex, the valuation question here is not whether cash flows exist but how long hyperscaler capex sustains them.
catalysts: Q2 FY2027 results (August 2026): guidance $91.0B +/-2% revenue at ~75% gross margin
GB300/NVLink ramp: networking revenue $11.0B (+263% y/y in Q4 FY26) becoming a second franchise
Any reopening of China datacenter compute (currently zero in outlook - pure upside option)
Capital returns: ~50% of FCF returned ($20B in Q1 alone)
risk_factors: Hyperscaler capex cycle: revenue is concentrated in a handful of AI spenders; a digestion year would compress both earnings and multiple simultaneously
Custom silicon (hyperscaler ASICs) eroding share of AI compute over the 5-year horizon
China: export restrictions already exclude China DC revenue; further escalation touches supply chains
Multiple compression has been the 2026 story: 29.8x trailing vs 44x average - the market is already voting for deceleration
Gaming supply constraints (management-flagged) and beta 2.22 in any risk-off tape

q1_fy2027_fcf.note: record quarterly FCF; $20B returned to shareholders; ~50% of FCF return policy
q1_fy2027_fcf.source: NVIDIA Q1 FY2027 press release / CFO commentary
